summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, recurrent urinary tract infections, and an indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted after a urine sample collected outpatient revealed growth of Klebsiella and Pseudomonas. He reported prior fevers and dysuria, but symptoms had resolved by admission and he remained asymptomatic. Infectious Disease was consulted and recommended against antibiotic treatment, as the findings were likely due to colonization rather than active infection, especially given a negative urine culture from a newly placed catheter. His sirolimus level was mildly elevated, but this was likely due to recent dosing; no adjustment was made, with plans to recheck as an outpatient. He remained stable throughout the hospitalization, with no need for medication changes or procedures. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor for urinary symptoms and to follow up with urology regarding intermittent catheterization to reduce future infection risk.
